mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises above 5%, but S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high unemployment indicates a supportive monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The specified conditions are met, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate during a tightening cycle leads to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate exceeds 4%, but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI growth is high, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production declines, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High employment numbers alongside low retail sales indicate economic imbalance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The specified conditions are met, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in housing starts during a late-cycle expansion signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts decline, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
